units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 4:1:27">Y. Ber. IV, 7ᶜ</cite> bot., a. e. <he>כ׳ נתפלל וכ׳</he> here (in this inn) did my father say the prayer of &c.
<cite ref="Mishnah Beitzah 4:7">Bets. IV, 7</cite> <he>מִכַּ׳ ועד כ׳</he> from here to there (will I use).
<cite ref="Mishnah Berakhot 1:2">Ber. I, 2</cite>, a. fr. <he>מכ׳ ואילך</he>, v. <cite ref="A01301"><he>אֵילֵךְ</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Sanhedrin 9:1">Snh. IX, 1</cite> <he>ולאחר מכ׳</he> and subsequently; a. fr.—<he>מכ׳ אמרו</he> (<he>חכמים</he>) from this originates what the scholars said.
<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 1:5">Ab. I, 5</cite>; a. fr.—<he>מִכַּ׳ ל־</he>, <he>מִכַּ׳ ש־</he> from this is derived, do we learn.
<cite ref="Berakhot 64a:6">Ber. 64ᵃ</cite> <he>מכ׳ לבעל וכ׳</he> from this (that Jacob is mentioned and not his ancestors) we learn that the owner of the beam must carry the heaviest side of it.

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 87a:2">B. Mets. 87ᵃ</cite> <he>מכ׳ שצדיקים אומרים וכ׳</he> from this we see that the righteous promise little &c.; a. fr.—<he>כ׳ … כ׳</he> here (in this case) …, there (in another place, in that case).
<cite ref="Sukkah 44b:1">Succ. 44ᵇ</cite>; a. v. fr.—Contr. <cite ref="K00825"><he>כַּן</he></cite>, with pref. <cite ref="M00000"><he>מ</he></cite>, <cite ref="M01410"><he>מִיכַּן</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 4:1:27">Y. Ber. IV, 7ᶜ</cite> top [read:] <he>כן ליחיד כן לציבור</he> in this case (when Levi disfavored many prayers), it is meant for individuals, in the other case, it is meant for congregations.—Y. Erub. VII, 24ᵇ bot. <he>מ׳ ומ׳</he> on both sides; a. fr.
